cards.front: What is the parameter passing mechanism in Java?
cards.back: Strictly pass-by-value — for primitives and for object references alike
cards.extra: There is no pass-by-reference in Java. The thing copied differs (a value or a reference), the mechanism does not.
cards.source: baeldung.com — Pass-By-Value as a Parameter Passing Mechanism in Java
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::02 Object Model::21 Pass by Value vs Pass by Reference
cards.example:
class Box { int n = 1; }
class Ex { static void bump(int x, Box b) { x++; b.n++; }
  static void m() { int x = 1; Box b = new Box(); bump(x, b); System.out.println(x + " " + b.n); } } // 1 2

cards.front: What exactly is copied when you pass an object to a method?
cards.back: The reference — a copy of the pointer, not the object it points to
cards.extra: Both the caller's variable and the parameter now refer to the same object on the heap. That is why mutations are visible.
cards.source: baeldung.com — Pass-By-Value as a Parameter Passing Mechanism in Java
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::02 Object Model::21 Pass by Value vs Pass by Reference
cards.example:
class Box { int n = 1; }
class Ex { static void f(Box b) { b = new Box(); b.n = 9; }
  static void m() { Box b = new Box(); f(b); System.out.println(b.n); } } // 1: pointer copy changed

cards.front: If a method mutates the object passed to it, does the caller see the change?
cards.back: Yes — because both references point at the same object
cards.extra: modify(a) calling a1.num++ changes the caller's object. This is what makes people believe Java is pass-by-reference.
cards.source: baeldung.com — Pass-By-Value as a Parameter Passing Mechanism in Java
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::02 Object Model::21 Pass by Value vs Pass by Reference
cards.example:
class Box { int n; }
class Ex { static void mutate(Box b) { b.n = 7; }
  static void demo() { Box shared = new Box(); mutate(shared); System.out.println(shared.n); } }

cards.front: If a method reassigns its object parameter, does the caller's variable change?
cards.back: No — the parameter is a separate variable holding a copy of the reference
cards.extra: b1 = new Foo() only repoints the local copy. The caller's variable still refers to the original object.
cards.source: baeldung.com — Pass-By-Value as a Parameter Passing Mechanism in Java
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::02 Object Model::21 Pass by Value vs Pass by Reference
cards.example:
class Box { int n; }
class Ex { static void reassign(Box p) { p = new Box(); p.n = 99; }
  static void demo() { Box b = new Box(); b.n = 1; reassign(b); System.out.println(b.n); } }

cards.front: Why can't you write a swap(a, b) method in Java?
cards.back: Because a method receives copies, so swapping the parameters has no effect on the caller's variables
cards.extra: This is the practical test of pass-by-reference: C++ can do it with &, Java cannot, for primitives or for references.
cards.source: baeldung.com — Pass-By-Value as a Parameter Passing Mechanism in Java
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::02 Object Model::21 Pass by Value vs Pass by Reference
cards.example:
class Ex { static void swap(int a, int b) { int t = a; a = b; b = t; }
  static void m() { int a = 1, b = 2; swap(a, b); System.out.println(a + " " + b); } } // 1 2

cards.front: How do Java's object references differ from C++ references?
cards.back: A Java reference behaves like a C++ pointer passed by value — you can mutate through it, but you cannot reseat the caller's variable
cards.extra: There is no equivalent of int& or Foo*&. Mutation works; reseating does not.
cards.source: baeldung.com — Pass-By-Value as a Parameter Passing Mechanism in Java
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::02 Object Model::21 Pass by Value vs Pass by Reference
cards.example:
class Box { int n; }
class Ex { static void reseat(Box b) { b = new Box(); }        // caller's variable unchanged
  static void mutate(Box b) { b.n = 7; }                      // caller sees this
  static void demo() { Box b = new Box(); reseat(b); mutate(b); System.out.println(b.n); } }

cards.back: In the callee's stack frame, and they disappear when the method returns
cards.extra: A local variable copy is reclaimed with the frame; the object it pointed at survives as long as something else references it.
cards.source: baeldung.com — Pass-By-Value as a Parameter Passing Mechanism in Java
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::02 Object Model::21 Pass by Value vs Pass by Reference
cards.example:
class Ex { static int twice(int n) { n = 2 * n; return n; }
  static void demo() { int x = 3; System.out.println(twice(x) + " " + x); } } // n dies with the frame
